title: `ValidationError` in AzureOpenAIEmbeddings when `OPENAI_API_BASE` is set
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Example Code

```python
import os
from langchain_openai import AzureOpenAIEmbeddings

os.environ["OPENAI_API_BASE"] = "foo"

embeddings = AzureOpenAIEmbeddings(
    api_key="my_api_key",
    azure_endpoint="https://myendpoint.com",
    model="azure.mymodel",
)
```


### Description

I'm using langchain_openai `AzureOpenAIEmbeddings`.
I expect `AzureOpenAIEmbeddings` is instantiated using `azure_endpoint` parameter value. I also expect to see an error message saying that the value of `azure_endpoint` can't be overridden when `OPENAI_API_BASE` is set if this is the case but I would also expect the user to be able to create an instance regardless of `OPENAI_API_BASE`.
Instead I see a validation error saying that I should specify Azure endpoint via the `azure_endpoint` which is already there. It's important because I'm using `OPENAI_API_BASE` env variable for different agents.

linked_prs.title: fix(openai): update `AzureOpenAIEmbeddings` validation logic for `openai_api_base`
linked_prs.body:
langchain_openai: only validate openai_api_base if azure_endpoint is not provided.
Fixes #31750

ai_judgment.response: Yes. This is an agent issue because it involves a misconfiguration related to an LLM provider (`AzureOpenAIEmbeddings`) and its parameters (`OPENAI_API_BASE` and `azure_endpoint`). Such misconfigurations fall under the "Model access misconfiguration" sub-category of LLM operation issues.
